facts.text: Rochdale AFC were founded in 1907 and have played at Spotland, now known as the Crown Oil Arena, ever since.
Dale returned to the Football League in May 2026, beating Boreham Wood on penalties at Wembley in the National League play-off final after finishing second with a club-record 106 points.
Rochdale had been relegated in 2023, ending 102 years as a Football League club, and spent three seasons in the National League before winning promotion back.
Dale's most famous recent FA Cup run came in 2018, when they drew 2-2 with Tottenham Hotspur at Spotland before losing the replay at Wembley.
Rochdale reached the League Cup final in 1962, losing 4-0 on aggregate to Norwich City.
Head coach Ian Watson took charge in summer 2026 after Jimmy McNulty, who led the promotion campaign, left for Stockport County.
The family of local businessman Peter Ogden completed a takeover of the club in May 2024; Simon Gauge and Cameron Ogden are co-chairmen.
Before 2010 Rochdale spent 36 consecutive seasons in the Football League's bottom division, a run that ended with promotion that year.

facts.text: Spotland, on Sandy Lane, has been a sports ground since 1878 and has carried the Crown Oil Arena name, after the Bury-based fuel company, since 2016.
Spotland holds 10,249 and is shared by Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Hornets, who moved there in 1988.
Rochdale AFC Women finished fifth in the North West Regional League Division One Central in 2025-26, with 10 wins from 18 games.

source.title: Rochdale AFC Women - Real Rochdale, summer 2026

facts.text: Rochdale AFC Women opened their last season with a fixture at the Crown Oil Arena, the club's Spotland home.

source.title: Rochdale AFC Women - Real Rochdale, summer 2026

facts.text: Rochdale Hornets were formed at the Roebuck Hotel on 20 April 1871 and were one of the 22 founder members of the Northern Union, rugby league's first governing body, in 1895.
The Hornets' only Challenge Cup final, in 1922, ended in a 10-9 win over Hull at Headingley.
Rochdale Hornets have had strong links with Fiji since the early 1960s, and Rochdale has a large Fijian community as a result.
The Hornets play in the Championship, rugby league's second tier, and share the Crown Oil Arena at Spotland with Rochdale AFC.
Rochdale Borough Council has 60 councillors, three for each of the borough's 20 wards, and is based at Number One Riverside in the town centre.
Rochdale Borough Council serves a borough of 223,773 people, according to the 2021 census.
The borough was formed in 1974 from Rochdale, Heywood, Middleton, Littleborough, Milnrow and Wardle.
Rochdale Town Hall, designed by William Henry Crossland, opened on 27 September 1871 and is Grade I listed.
Rochdale Town Hall closed in 2020 for a conservation project that ran until 2024, and the restoration won a Europa Nostra Award in 2026.
Rochdale Town Hall's original clock tower spire burned down in 1883; the stone tower that replaced it, by Alfred Waterhouse, was finished in 1887.
Rochdale Riverside, the £80 million shopping and leisure scheme on the edge of the town centre, opened its first phase in April 2020.
Rochdale Riverside's anchor tenants are a 50,000 sq ft Marks & Spencer and a six-screen Reel Cinema.
Metrolink trams reached Rochdale railway station in February 2013 and Rochdale Town Centre, the end of the line, in March 2014.
Full-route trams run between Rochdale Town Centre and East Didsbury, calling at Newhey, Milnrow, Kingsway Business Park and Newbold within the borough.
Freehold tram stop, between South Chadderton and Oldham town centre, was built new on the trackbed of the old railway line.
Heywood lies four miles south-west of Rochdale and grew as a cotton mill town from the late 18th century.
Heywood station, closed in 1970, reopened in 2003 on the East Lancashire Railway heritage line.
Heywood's Queens Park reopened in 2006 after a multimillion-pound restoration of its Victorian fountain and statues.
Heywood's best-known landmark is the parish church of St Luke, whose spire stands 188 feet tall.
Heywood Civic Centre reopened in February 2026 after a multi-million pound refurbishment funded by Rochdale Borough Council and Arts Council England, and is run by Your Trust.

source.title: First look: Inside Heywood's revamped civic - Rochdale Borough Council

facts.text: The refurbished Heywood Civic Centre added a glass-fronted bar and cafe and a Changing Places facility, and is home to the arts organisation Cartwheel Arts.

source.title: First look: Inside Heywood's revamped civic - Rochdale Borough Council

facts.text: Middleton's parish church of St Leonard, finished in 1524, holds the Flodden Window, thought to be the UK's oldest war memorial.
The radical writer Samuel Bamford led a Middleton contingent to St Peter's Fields in 1819, the meeting that ended in the Peterloo Massacre.
Middleton lies about five miles from both Manchester and Rochdale.
Littleborough, three miles north-east of Rochdale, sits at the Summit Gap, the low pass chosen for both the Rochdale Canal and the Manchester to Leeds railway across the Pennines.
Hollingworth Lake, on the south side of Littleborough, was built around 1800 to feed the Rochdale Canal and became a country park in 1974.
Hollingworth Lake was completed in 1800 as a reservoir to feed the Rochdale Canal, and Rochdale Council made it a country park in 1974.
Captain Matthew Webb trained on the lake before becoming the first person to swim the English Channel in 1875.
Milnrow, about two miles east of Rochdale town centre, sits beside junction 21 of the M62 and has had its own Metrolink stop since 2013.
Newhey is home to the Ellenroad Engine House, which preserves what is described as the world's largest working steam mill engine.
The 18th-century dialect writer John Collier, known as Tim Bobbin, was Milnrow's schoolmaster from 1739 until his death in 1786.
Rochdale Foodbank was started in 2012 by local churches and community groups with £400 and six people, and now relies on more than 100 volunteers.
Rochdale Foodbank is based at 14-16 Newgate in the town centre and also distributes food on Saturdays in Smallbridge.
Springhill Hospice opened on 8 October 1989 after a public appeal led by founder Margaret Geoghegan raised the £1.5 million needed to build and equip it.

source.title: Hospice Chair looks back on 30 years of care - ehospice

facts.text: Springhill Hospice, on Broad Lane, provides an inpatient unit, day services, care at home and bereavement support for people across the borough.
The museum at 31 Toad Lane is the building where the Rochdale Pioneers opened their co-operative shop on 21 December 1844.

source.title: About Toad Lane - Rochdale Pioneers Museum

facts.text: The Toad Lane building first opened as a museum in 1931 and reopened in October 2012 after a redevelopment; its front room recreates the original 1844 store.

source.title: About Toad Lane - Rochdale Pioneers Museum

facts.text: Hopwood Hall College has campuses in Rochdale and Middleton and was incorporated in 1992, bringing together Rochdale's further education, art and technology colleges.
Rochdale Rugby Union Football Club was founded in 1921 and plays at Bamford, at the top of Moorgate Avenue off Bury Road.
